title: #001. Ice Cream Production Mix
subtitle: Translate a plain business problem into decision variables, constraints, and an objective — where greedy loses to LP.
markdown:
# #001. Ice Cream Production Mix

<!-- section:scenario -->
An artisan creamery manufactures $n$ flavors of bulk gelato (sold by the liter as **continuous** non-negative quantities `quantities[j] >= 0`). Each batch is constrained by $m$ shared ingredients and kitchen capacities `capacities[k]`, where producing 1 liter of flavor $j$ consumes `usages[k][j]` units of resource $k$ and yields unit profit `margins[j]`.

Determine how many liters of each flavor to produce in order to **maximize total profit**.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P001Input`)**:
  - `margins: number[]` — profit per unit of product $j$ ($0 \le j < n$)
  - `usages: number[][]` — resource matrix where `usages[k][j]` is resource $k$ required per unit of product $j$
  - `capacities: number[]` — available capacity of each resource $k$ ($0 \le k < m$)
- **Output (`P001Output`)**:
  - `quantities: number[]` — non-negative continuous production amounts of length $n$
  - `totalProfit: number` — maximized profit $\sum_j \text{margins}[j] \cdot \text{quantities}[j]$

<!-- section:example -->
Suppose flavor 0 earns `500`/L (using `3` milk, `1` sugar) and flavor 1 earns `300`/L (using `1` milk, `2` sugar), with `90` milk and `80` sugar available:

- **Greedy temptation**: Prioritize only flavor 0 because its `500`/L margin is higher. Milk caps flavor 0 at `90 / 3 = 30` L, leaving `50` sugar unused for a profit of only **`15,000`**.
- **Optimal LP blend**: Producing `quantities = [20, 30]` uses all `90` milk and `80` sugar simultaneously for **`19,000`** profit — `4,000` higher than greedy!

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Translate the scenario into the three core elements of an LP model:
1. **Decision variables**: continuous variables $x_j \ge 0$ for each flavor $j$.
2. **Constraints**: one linear `<=` inequality per resource $k$ summing `usages[k][j] * x[j]`.
3. **Objective**: `maximize` the inner product `dot(margins, x)`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Don't round `quantities` to integers here! Resource allocations of bulk volume are continuous (`m.continuous` / `h.addVariable`), and in Case 2 the exact LP vertex has fractional quantities (`[6.666..., 46.666..., 0]`) yielding `28666.67`! Forcing integrality would artificially cut off the true optimum and trigger `SUBOPTIMAL`.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max \quad & \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} c_j x_j \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} a_{k,j} x_j \le b_k && \forall k \in \{0, \dots, m-1\} \\
& x_j \ge 0 && \forall j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}
\end{aligned}
$$

Real business translation begins by explicitly mapping every noun phrase into `(index sets, parameters, decision variables, constraints, objective)`. Here, greedy marginal sorting fails whenever multiple resources bottleneck together.

judge.m0: Output must be an object { quantities, totalProfit }.
judge.m3: Reported totalProfit ({p0}) does not match computed margin sum ({p1}).
judge.m4: Feasible production plan, but profit ({p0}) is below the LP optimum ({p1}).
